newsitem.title: USA: Aetna, other HMOs down after rate proposal.
newsitem.headline: Aetna, other HMOs down after rate proposal.

text.p: Shares of Aetna Inc and other HMO stocks moved lower on Friday after investors reassessed an HMO rate hike proposed by the Clinton Administration, Wall Street analysts said.
HMO stocks rallied late Thursday on the news of the proposal, but the stocks retreated Friday as investors took the view that the final rate is likely to be lower, analysts said.
Meanwhile, news of Richard Huber's appointment as president and chief executive officer of Aetna was viewed as a positive, analysts said.
"If anything, this is a positive because it removes the uncertainty associated with trying to pick someone," CS First Boston analyst Joe France said.
Analysts said Huber's appointment did not come as a surprise and said they had confidence in his management ability.

"Anytime you bring in an outside CEO, it can bring a fresh perspective," Dillon Read analyst Jim Lane said. But, he said, in Aetna's case, an outside CEO might disrupt the, so far, successful integration of U.S. Healthcare, which Aetna acquired last year.
"The important thing is it makes the CEO (appointment) a non-event rather than some kind of controversial topic," Lane said."
Aetna Inc fell 2-12/16, or more than two percent, to 112-5/16, Humana Inc fell one, or more than four percent, to 23-1/2 and Oxford Health Plans Inc fell 1-3/8, or about 1.5 percent, to 86-1/8.
